title: Stochastic Diversity Stabilization in Nonlinear Competitive Dynamics: A Statistical Mechanics Approach to Fluctuation Suppression and Finite-Size Scaling
comment: 38 pages, 8 figures (including supplementary material). Accepted manuscript of the article published in Physica A 701 (2026) 132041
summary: Stochastic forcing can prevent diversity collapse in competitive dynamical systems, yet the quantitative conditions and the dynamical mechanism responsible remain poorly characterized. We address both questions in a class of nonlinear stochastic replicator dynamics on the N-dimensional probability simplex, parameterized by a nonlinearity exponent gamma and additive Gaussian noise of intensity sigma. Under the baseline interaction, the minimum noise required to sustain diversity decays as a power law, sigma_c ~ N^(-alpha); replacing the baseline interaction with a superlinear variant shifts alpha from about 1.1 to about 2.0, in agreement with a linear-stability prediction alpha = (gamma+2)/2, identifying alpha as a model-specific quantity rather than a universal index. Scanning the (gamma, sigma) plane reveals a smooth dynamical crossover: the fluctuation susceptibility chi_H = N Var(H) peaks at gamma ~ 0.7 (chi_H ~ 0.6) and is suppressed at high gamma, with no divergence near gamma ~ 1.4; matched finite-size analysis finds no systematic divergence of the peak with N, ruling out a genuine second-order phase transition. The entropy relaxation time tau_relax(gamma) remains approximately constant (about 2.9 time units) across the full range of gamma, even as chi_H decreases sixfold; this decoupling between relaxation timescale and fluctuation amplitude implies that suppression arises from convergence of diverse pathways to similar endpoints rather than from accelerated relaxation along a single channel. These findings identify nonlinear fluctuation suppression via pathway multiplicity -- distinct from both noise-induced transitions and equilibrium criticality -- as the operative stabilization pattern in this class of nonequilibrium stochastic systems.

title: Resonant-pair energy return beyond the early Green-Kubo plateau in a quartic chain
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables; includes supplementary material and machine-readable source data
summary: Distinguishing rapid local energy exchange from sustained transport matters when thermal conductivity is inferred from finite simulations. In a weakly coupled chain of separable quartic oscillators, we identify a quantitative mechanism that changes an early Green--Kubo plateau: resonant neighbors exchange energy and coherently return it. The pair heat-current integral maps to the classical pendulum trapping response. Quartic homogeneity gives an energy-independent reference period $T_{\rm lib}=7.77ε^{-1/2}$, where $ε$ is the coupling. Without fitted parameters, the leading response predicts a negative first minimum at $0.952T_{\rm lib}$ with depth $-0.74$ times the independent-cell exchange coefficient. Isolated-pair simulations test this reference and resolve finite-coupling corrections. The chain reaches its first minimum on the same time scale, with a shallower minimum and a small later residual. Comparisons with chaotic cells and energy-conserving noise show regimes in which coherent return is absent or interrupted over the measured windows. These finite-time results provide a quantitative reference for separating the early exchange plateau from subsequent correlated dynamics.

title: Foresight-dependent entropy production in stochastic two-agent dynamics
summary: Nonreciprocal interactions can break detailed balance by sustaining stationary probability currents. Here we ask whether such currents can also emerge when the agents' immediate coordination preferences are reciprocal, but their state-adjustment rules are determined by forward-looking optimization (foresight). We study a minimal stochastic linear-quadratic game in which two agents control noisy scalar states and minimize individual discounted costs in a full-information feedback Nash equilibrium. The optimized controls yield an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process whose stationary probability current and entropy-production rate, measuring statistical time-irreversibility, can be calculated exactly. For reciprocal coordination with unequal self-anchoring strengths, the effective drift asymmetry first appears at order $τ^5$, where $τ$ is the planning timescale, and the normalized entropy production consequently scales as $τ^8$ in the limit $τ\to0$. We derive this cancellation from the coupled Nash Riccati equations. For conformist-contrarian coupling, normalized entropy production approaches a nonzero short-foresight limit and initially decreases from that limit by an amount proportional to $τ^2$. We also determine the long-foresight limit for a conformist-contrarian pair with equal self-anchoring strengths. Numerical solutions of the full Nash equations verify the asymptotic laws and reveal the effect of foresight. Thus, forward-looking optimization can generate or reduce normalized stationary irreversibility, depending on the underlying interaction.

title: Einstein's theory of Brownian motion: The non-Fickian normal diffusion
summary: Einstein's theory of diffusion defines what is considered {\it normal diffusion}. Historically, Einstein considered homogeneous diffusion characterised by a diffusion constant in his original calculations, resulting in what is known as {\it Fickian} diffusion, which thermally relaxes concentration inhomogeneities. However, in the same derivation of Einstein, the seed of generalisation of the theory to {\it non-Fickian} diffusion in the presence of space-dependent diffusivity is hidden. This indicates that non-Fickian diffusion, which can drive concentration inhomogeneities, can also be normal diffusion. The present article discusses the origin of the {\it normal} non-Fickian diffusion in Einstein's theory of diffusion.

title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
summary: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

title: Flexible Proposal Distributions for Gravitational-Wave Population Inference with Gaussian Mixture Models
summary: Population analyses of gravitational-wave (GW) sources use hierarchical Bayesian inference to constrain astrophysical models while accounting for selection effects. The likelihood is usually estimated by Monte Carlo integration over finite sets of event posterior samples and simulated injections. As catalogs grow, more samples are needed to control the Monte Carlo variance, but the available event samples are fixed by parameter estimation. Sharp population features can also lie in regions poorly sampled by the event posteriors. We fit Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to the event posteriors and evaluate the likelihood by importance sampling with two proposals: an ensemble of event posteriors and a mixture of that ensemble with a fiducial population. Together with a GMM representation of detected injections, this allows additional samples to be drawn for both event and selection integrals. Increasing the sample count reduces Monte Carlo variance but leaves uncertainty from fitting the densities to finite training sets. In simulated catalogs, the GMM-based estimators show no detectable additional bias relative to the posterior-sample estimator; their calibration is comparable within the limitations of the tests. An application to GWTC-3 with a different mass model gives consistent results across the estimators. The method separates the numerical sampling budget from the original sample count, while requiring explicit checks of density-fit uncertainty and approximation error.

title: Natural Chlorine Enhances Antineutrino Detection in the Deep Ocean
summary: Large-volume neutrino telescopes such as IceCube and KM3NeT exploit natural ice or water as detection media, but their sparse instrumentation makes MeV neutrino interactions difficult to identify individually. We show that chlorine naturally abundant in seawater provides an intrinsic neutron-capture target that enables efficient tagging of electron antineutrinos through inverse beta decay. In contrast to the 2.2 MeV $γ$-ray from neutron capture on hydrogen, capture on chlorine produces an $\sim$8.6 MeV $γ$-ray cascade on a shorter time scale, yielding a distinctive delayed-coincidence signature. Using measured seawater properties at the TRIDENT site and a detector-level simulation, we find that chlorine-assisted tagging can extend the core-collapse supernova 5$σ$ discovery reach from $\sim$50 to over 100 kpc. We validate the underlying detection principle with a salted-water experiment at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory, observing correlated neutron-capture signatures under suppressed cosmic muon background conditions. Natural seawater thus transforms the deep ocean into an intrinsically enhanced antineutrino detection medium, opening new opportunities for MeV neutrino astronomy and distributed measurements of reactor and geophysical antineutrinos.

title: Twisted scattering from Chern-Simons theory
summary: We consider boundary conditions of two-dimensional Dirac fermions which preserve a non-anomalous continuous symmetry which acts differently on the left- and right-movers. Such boundaries are equivalent to topological defects of Weyl fermions preserving the symmetry. We give a general construction of such defects for conformally-embedded symmetries using Chern-Simons theory. They always exist and can be realised as half-space gauging defects for some finite categorical symmetry. Using this technology, we compute the twist lines to which fermions become attached upon scattering through the defect, the boundary central charge of the corresponding folded boundary state, and its mod-2 valued SPT class. As applications, we first consider abelian symmetries and find agreement with known results in the literature. We then study a novel example where an $SU(2) \times SU(4) \times U(1)^2$ symmetry is preserved. In contrast to the abelian case, the twist lines are intrinsically non-invertible and belong to either a $\text{TY}(\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_3)$ or $\text{Rep}(\mathbb{S}_3) \times \mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry depending on whether scattering is to the left or the right.

title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
summary: Donor substitution can tune the coupled ferroelectric, dielectric, electronic, and optical properties of perovskite oxides by modifying lattice distortions and electronic screening. We investigate these effects in La-doped BaTiO3 using density functional theory, density-functional perturbation theory, and the Berry-phase formalism for polarization. For a model with 12.5% La substitution at the Ba site, La incorporation induces anisotropic lattice contraction, reduces tetragonality and Ti off-centering, and weakens the energetic stabilization of the tetragonal ferroelectric phase. The accompanying reduction in polarization is associated with enhanced electronic screening and reduced anomalous Born effective charges. Phonon calculations indicate that the relaxed doped structure is dynamically stable, while hardening of a low-frequency polar mode is consistent with weakened ferroelectricity. The high-frequency dielectric response increases moderately, whereas the static dielectric response decreases as the lattice contribution is suppressed. Electronic-structure calculations show a Fermi-level shift toward the conduction band without mid-gap defect states. The optical spectra exhibit an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein-Moss-type mechanism, enhanced near-edge transparency, and reduced birefringence. Together, these results suggest a microscopic connection between donor-induced screening, polar-mode hardening, reduced dynamical charges, polarization suppression, and decreased optical anisotropy. The conclusions apply to the investigated 12.5% composition; calculations at additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.

title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
summary: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

title: Partial geometrization of dark matter in metric $f(R)$ gravity: Exact reconstruction and growth constraints
summary: We ask what fraction of dark matter can be accounted for by the geometry of a stable metric $f(R)$ theory, requiring the expansion history to be exactly equal to that of the $Λ$CDM model. Only a fraction $ξ$ of dark matter clusters as dust, whereas $f(R)$ supplies the rest, as well as $Λ$. We show that the background reconstruction reduces to a linear equation for $F\equiv f_R$, whose solution is $F-1=(1-ξ)\,Θ(a)$, with $Θ$ independent of $ξ$: the departure from general relativity is exactly proportional to the geometrized fraction. We solve this equation in closed form in the matter$+Λ$ and radiation$+$matter eras: in both, the solution is an elementary particular solution plus two hypergeometric modes. Stability requires $F$ to decrease monotonically in time, so $F$ cannot take its general-relativity value $F=1$ both at early and at late times. The effective gravitational coupling $G/F$ therefore necessarily runs: between the radiation era and the de Sitter attractor, $F$ changes by at least $0.837\,(1-ξ)$. In all stable reconstructions but one, $F-1$ grows as $R^{1/3}$ at high curvature, i.e., in dense environments such as the Sun, and local tests of gravity exclude them. The surviving member has $F\to1$ at early times: it recovers general relativity at high curvature and attains the minimal running of $F$. Keeping the linear growth factor at $k=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ within $10\%$ of its $Λ$CDM value requires $1-ξ\lesssim10^{-3}$, the weakest bound among all stable reconstructions; keeping $σ_8$ within $3\%$ requires $1-ξ\lesssim5\times10^{-5}$. Growth-rate data from DESI DR1 and SDSS DR16 give $1-ξ\lesssim10^{-3}$--$10^{-2}$, and the Cassini bound gives $1-ξ\lesssim10^{-10}$. A smoothly evolving metric $f(R)$ background can therefore geometrize only a negligible fraction of dark matter.

title: CURTAIN: Towards a Foundation Model for Neutrino Telescopes
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Representations for the Physical Sciences
summary: Neutrino telescopes record more than a trillion photon detections per year, yet there does not exist a self-supervised learning (SSL) task which fully satisfies all three conditions: improving as the pretraining set grows, transferring to a different detector, and outperforming the best model trained without pretraining at all. We introduce CURTAIN, a temporal masking scheme and the first SSL task for neutrino telescopes that achieves all of these goals. Downstream performance monotonically improves with the number of pretraining events, as predicted by scaling laws. Our encoder builds on DeepIce, currently the leading model on the NuBench benchmarks direction reconstruction task. Pretraining it with CURTAIN reduces its median angular error by 45% and its median energy error by 31% compared to training from scratch. It also transfers to a detector geometry never seen in pretraining, reducing the median angular error by 36% compared to training from scratch. At matched capacity and pretraining data, CURTAIN-pretrained encoders beat those pretrained by existing SSL tasks on both tasks and at every pretraining set size.

title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.

title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
summary: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.

title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
summary: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

title: Wormhole geometries and energy conditions in linear and non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity
summary: This study explores static and spherically symmetric wormhole configurations in an extended formulation of symmetric teleparallel gravity governed by $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m $ and $f(Q,L_m)= -Q+L_m^α $ (where $Q$ is the non-metricity scalar, $L_m$ is the matter Lagrangian, and $α, β$ are constants). By varying the action with respect to the metric, we obtain the corresponding field equations. We conclude that the linear $f(Q,L_m)=α(-Q)+βL_m$ framework successfully supports physically realistic wormholes without requiring extreme energy condition violations. It has been demonstrated that spacetime solutions violating both the radial and lateral null energy conditions in general relativity can nevertheless satisfy the NEC in $f(Q, L_m)$ gravity. Within non-linear $f(Q,L_m)$ gravity, non-exotic asymptotically flat wormhole solutions are derived using linear and asymptotically linear equations of state. Our results open new avenues to link modified gravity models with the observable astrophysical traits of exotic spacetimes.

title: Precise Measurement of the Inclusive Cross Sections of Open-Charm Mesons at Energies from 3.80 to 4.95 GeV
summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies from $3.80$ to $4.95~\text{GeV}$, the inclusive production cross sections of open-charm mesons, $σ(e^{+}e^{-}\to D^{0}/D^{+}/D_{s}^{+}+X)$, are measured by tagging a $D^0$, $D^+$, or $D_s^+$ meson, where $X$ denotes any accompanying particles. Open-charm production dominates the total hadronic yield above threshold. Therefore these measurements provide a vital reference for understanding hadron production and for validating global $R$ value results. The results offer crucial inputs for investigating heavier charmonia and exotic states coupled to open-charm final states, while serving as a benchmark for comparison with the sum of measured exclusive channels. This comparison directly evaluates the completeness of current exclusive datasets and clarifies the underlying hadronization mechanisms in the open-charm region.

title: Collinear Gluons from Gravity: Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt Decomposition and Twisted Intersections
summary: We give an explicit reconstruction of subleading collinear Yang--Mills amplitudes from one-graviton amplitudes in Einstein--Yang--Mills theory and its string corrections. We realize the monodromy kernel in the mixed open-closed string relation as a weighted Lie-algebraic recursion on words of gluon labels. At order $α'^r$, its output contains at most $r$ Lie factors. The Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) theorem decomposes the space spanned by gluon orderings into sectors whose dimensions are given by unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind. Appropriate shuffle sums of one-graviton amplitudes extract the degree-$r$ sector, for which the string-period matrix drops out. Accordingly, we show that the reconstruction coefficients factor into linear kinematic factors over the product of bipartition factors. Finally, we express the reconstruction coefficients as twisted intersection numbers between Parke--Taylor forms and explicit forest cocycles constructed recursively from logarithmic four-point differentials.

title: Nature of the bosonic edge phase in a double quantum spin Hall insulator
summary: Field-theoretic analysis has predicted that the edge of a double quantum spin Hall insulator (DQSHI) can undergo an interaction-driven transition from a phase with fermionic edge modes into one with only bosonic modes. All single-fermion edge excitations are gapped in this bosonic edge phase, but fermion pairs remain gapless, leading to distinct experimental signatures. We numerically simulate the interacting DQSHI edge and verify the existence of the bosonic edge phase. This calculation requires an explicit bulk embedding of the DQSHI edge, due to its mixed anomaly between charge and $S^z$ conservation. We hence employ segment DMRG on an infinite two-dimensional cylinder, where the DQSHI bulk is modeled in terms of two copies of the spin-up lowest Landau level, combined with their time-reversed counterparts. We find that interactions can open a single-fermion gap at the DQSHI edge while fermion pairs remain gapless, matching the predictions for the bosonic edge phase. We find the scaling of the single-fermion gap with interaction strength to be consistent with field-theoretic calculations, and discuss the relevance of the bosonic edge phase to twisted homobilayers of WSe$_2$ and MoTe$_2$. We elaborate on the methodological extension of the segment geometry used here to other topological phases with edge anomalies.

title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
summary: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.

title: Ricci-flat Seeds, Trombone Rescaling and Magnetizing Kerr Black Holes
summary: We present a new family of Ricci-flat rotating metrics, which we refer to as Solution II, obtained by demagnetizing the genuine Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (G-KBR) black hole. Together with Solution I, which was previously obtained by demagnetizing the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) black hole, this gives two families of Ricci-flat deformations of the Kerr black hole, each labeled by $B$. We study the global structures, thermodynamics, various limits, and the local connections among these limits. We also study the remagnetizations in both Einstein-Maxwell and Kaluza-Klein theories, and find that, to yield a physically acceptable solution, the Ernst transformation should be augmented by an appropriate trombone rescaling.

title: Measurements of the branching fractions of $Λ_c^+\toΛK^+ π^0$ and $Λ_c^+\toΛK^+ η$ decays at Belle and Belle II
summary: We present a study of the three-body, singly Cabibbo-suppressed decays $Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ π^0$ and $Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ η$ using data recorded with the Belle and Belle II detectors at the KEKB and SuperKEKB $e^+ e^-$ colliders. The data samples correspond to integrated luminosities of 980$\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ and 570$\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, respectively. We measure their branching-fraction ratios relative to the Cabibbo-favored decay $Λ_c^+ \to Λπ^+ π^0$ as $\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ π^0)/\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to Λπ^+ π^0)=(1.82 \pm 0.07 \pm 0.07)\%$, with significantly improved precision compared to the previous measurement, and $\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ η)/\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to Λπ^+ π^0)=(8.73 \pm 0.35 \pm 0.43)\times10^{-3}$, corresponding to the first observation of the $Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ η$ decay with a statistical significance exceeding 10 standard deviations. The first and second uncertainties are statistical and systematic, respectively. Using the world-average value of the branching fraction for $Λ_c^+ \to Λπ^+ π^0$, we obtain the branching fractions $\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ π^0)=(1.29\pm 0.05\pm 0.05\pm 0.06)\times10^{-3}$ and $\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to ΛK^+ η)=(6.20\pm 0.25\pm 0.31\pm 0.30)\times10^{-4}$, where the third uncertainty arises from the uncertainty in the world-average value of $\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+ \to Λπ^+ π^0)$. The measured $\mathcal{B}(Λ_c^+\toΛK^+η)$ is significantly larger than predictions based on $SU(3)$ flavor symmetry.

title: Reentrant $d=2+1$ Superfluidity at High Temperature
summary: We present a UV-complete model with a global $U(1)$ symmetry in $d=2+1$ dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T\to\infty$.

title: Discrete time liquids
comment: 8 pages main + 9 pages supplement, 4 figures main + 10 figures supplement
summary: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.

title: First-order differential constraints for the nonlinear wave equation:wave fronts, admissible nonlinearities and exact solutions
summary: We construct exact solutions of the nonlinear wave equation in three space dimensions by the method of linear determining equations: first-order constraint functions are found as solutions of the linear determining equation, the differential constraints obtained by setting them equal to zero are integrated, and the resulting ansatz is substituted into the equation. Lie point symmetries are a special case, and the solutions obtained generically have no symmetry. The determining equations tie the admissible nonlinearity to the geometry of the constraint: arbitrary on characteristic hyperplanes, cubic on light cones, and, for a pair of constraints, exponential on light cones and quintic on the cylindrical fronts of a line source. Among the solutions are smooth bounded sine-Gordon walls and vortex configurations whose shape varies arbitrarily along a front, the fields of point sources moving on arbitrary trajectories for the cubic and Liouville equations, with an exact nonlinear analogue of the Larmor formula for the power radiated in the cubic case, and smooth finite-energy solutions of the cubic equation with any prescribed number of toroidal nodal surfaces.

title: Calculating gravitational waves at infinity: the missing link
summary: Gravitational-wave science requires waveform templates to be computed at future null infinity, the asymptotic boundary of spacetime. Numerical solutions of Einstein's equations typically rely on a Cauchy evolution on a finite computational domain, but can produce waveforms at infinity by performing a subsequent characteristic evolution that compactifies the spacetime. Such waveforms capture expected physical effects, like gravitational-wave memory and late-time, power-law tails. But this characteristic evolution requires initial data consistent with the interior Cauchy solution to avoid producing spurious, long-lived transients. A careful analysis shows that previous prescriptions for this initial data were not sufficiently consistent and provides a way to remedy the problem. The new initial data yield accurate waveforms from the first cycle onward. The construction is independent of the Cauchy formulation and enables the production of catalogs of robust waveforms at infinity.

title: A superconducting LC resonator in a multi-tesla magnetic field for tabletop kHz gravitational-wave detection
summary: We present a concept for a superconducting inductance--capacitance (LC) resonator immersed in a magnetic field for gravitational-wave detection in the kHz band. In the long-wavelength limit, a gravitational wave in a static magnetic field induces an oscillating magnetic-field perturbation proportional to the static magnetic field applied to the resonator and to the gravitational-wave strain. We show that a superconducting pickup circuit can convert this perturbation into a flux signal read out by a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID)-based or quantum-limited amplifier chain. Inspired by resonant-mass detectors, we develop a three-loop coupled-circuit model and derive the equivalent strain-noise spectrum, including thermal noise, SQUID backaction, and measurement imprecision. Prototype measurements demonstrate a quality factor of $Q\simeq 5\times 10^5$, while $Q=10^7$ is considered as a future development target. Under the assumed flux coupling and an idealized quantum-limited SQUID noise model, optimized circuits yield projected strain sensitivities of order $10^{-21}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$ over $100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ bands in the $1$--$20\,\mathrm{kHz}$ range. Increasing the active high-field volume and improving quantum-limited readout could enable further sensitivity gains. This compact, tunable detector concept could complement interferometric gravitational-wave searches and motivate investigations of high-frequency astrophysical sources.

title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
comment: 81 pages, 34 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook in the ancillary files
summary: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.

title: Charge-monitored Luttinger liquid
summary: We discuss phases of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids without particle number conservation, such as those in proximity to a superconductor, subjected to weak continuous measurements of their particle density, in the regime where the bosonization approach is applicable. We show that the phases of these systems are controlled by the competition between measurements, which favor the area-law phase and particle tunneling in and out of the Luttinger liquid, which favors the volume-law phase. The volume-law phase in this system is always charge fuzzy. We show that within this framework, the phase boundary between the two phases is given by a universal dependence of the Luttinger parameter on the measurement rate. This behavior can be contrasted with the non-universal phase boundaries in more generic highly excited one dimensional systems whose behavior is no longer captured by the Luttinger liquid framework.

title: A sharp gradient-corrected Lieb--Thirring inequality in one dimension with applications to density functional theory
summary:
We first prove a sharp Lieb-Thirring inequality with semi-classical constant and gradient correction in one dimension. In the periodic setting, the corresponding inequality also includes a parity dependent shell-correction term, which appears to be new. Moreover, we also characterize the optimizers of these inequalities. In particular, the optimizing density profiles form a two-dimensional manifold, which we call here the Poincaré density manifold.
  We then apply these results to study the Thomas--Fermi--von Weizsäcker (TFW) approximation of the kinetic energy in Density Functional Theory. More precisely, we first obtain an explicit and non-asymptotic bound on the global and local error made by the TFW approximation. These bounds are controlled by the distance of the normalized density profile from the Poincaré density manifold times the number of particles. In particular, these bounds show that the TFW approximation is exact on the Poincaré manifold. We then show that, in the periodic setting, the distance between the Kohn-Sham potential and the inverse TFW potential in the natural dual Sobolev space can also be controlled by explicit density dependent constants times the distance to the Poincaré manifold. As a corollary, we prove that for a fixed density profile, the Kohn-Sham potential converges towards the inverse Thomas--Fermi potential in the high-density limit $N \rightarrow \infty$ with asymptotic rate of order $N^{-2}$. This rate is shown to be optimal.

title: Accurate initial data for Cauchy-characteristic evolution
summary: Accurate gravitational-wave (GW) templates from numerical-relativity (NR) simulations are essential for GW science. These templates are typically computed at finite radii and extrapolated to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^{+}$, the asymptotic boundary of spacetime. However, this procedure is known to not accurately capture momentum fluxes and memory effects, limiting the accuracy of waveform models and data analyses that rely on them. Cauchy-characteristic evolution (CCE) instead integrates Einstein's equations along outgoing null hypersurfaces from a Cauchy simulation's finite-radius worldtube to $\mathscr{I}^{+}$. Its accuracy, though, has been limited by initial data that produce long-lived spurious transients, which contaminate several cycles of the waveform emitted by the binary coalescence. We identify incorrect initial angular coordinates as the source of these transients. We construct initial data that matches the Cauchy worldtube data through second order in the radial derivatives and solve for the angular coordinates consistent with the resulting radial profile. These improvements remove the unphysical transient: a $10\%$ modulation of a binary black hole's $(2,2)$ mode amplitude lasting over $1000\,M$ disappears, and the late-time tail of a head-on black hole collision is recovered. The construction is independent of the Cauchy formulation and allows archived simulations to be reprocessed with CCE, paving the way for improved GW catalogs.

title: Probing imperfect axions with nuclear clocks
summary: We show that $^{229}$Th nuclear clocks can probe departures from the Peccei-Quinn (PQ) solution to the strong CP problem. Explicit PQ breaking or additional CP-violating interactions can shift the minimum of the axion potential and generate CP-violating couplings to matter, inducing a clock response linear in the axion field. We investigate explicit PQ breaking and quark chromo-electric dipole operators as representative realizations of these \textit{imperfect axion} scenarios, consistent with electric dipole moment constraints. For axion dark matter, the linear signal oscillates at the Compton frequency and can dominate the quadratic response. Even without axion dark matter, the Earth can source a static axion field, enabling fifth-force searches with nuclear clocks.

title: From bulk flows to boundary generators and costs
summary: Holographic complexity admits a broad family of bulk observables, yet their relation to boundary state-preparation costs remains unclear. We propose a local prescription that associates suitable bulk observables with quadratic cost geometries on families of states prepared by Euclidean sources. Building on the holographic transport of bulk Hamiltonian flows to Euclidean preparation sources, we use the Hessian of the transported generator at a stationary reference state to define a candidate cost metric. When this Hessian is positive definite, the minimised preparation energy reproduces the change in the bulk observable to quadratic order. We characterise the resulting preparation penalties relative to the Fubini-Study metric and compute them for the maximal volume in scalar perturbations of AdS$_3$. At large-conformal dimension, we recover the known proportionality between cost and Fubini-Study metrics. At finite dimension, we obtain positive but generally unequal penalties for source variations that displace the bulk field and its conjugate momentum, breaking this proportionality even for a single scalar operator. We further study a deformation of volume by quadratic scalar and gradient terms in the large-dimension regime, determining how the couplings modify the penalties and constrain positivity. These additions selectively change field-displacement costs, with the gradient term introducing mode dependence. Our results provide an explicit local connection between the choice of bulk observables and the assignment of boundary preparation penalties.

title: Charge Density Waves and In-Gap States in Coupled Chains and Moiré Superlattices
summary: Charge density waves (CDWs) arise from the interplay between electrons and lattice distortions and are a hallmark of low-dimensional systems. Here we study coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains, both lattice-matched ladders and lattice-mismatched moiré superlattices, and find a rich set of CDW phases together with symmetry-protected bound states. In lattice-matched chains, the competition between electron-phonon coupling and interchain tunneling drives a sequence of CDW phases, including staggered dimers, trimers, and incommensurate states. These phases are generally gapped and host bound states protected by crystalline symmetries rather than chiral symmetry, and are therefore not pinned to zero energy. Lattice mismatch further reconstructs these phases into long-period supermoiré CDWs, with an ordered array of defects, pinned to the moiré length scale, that host localized electronic states. Interchain tunneling and lattice mismatch thus emerge as natural control parameters for CDW order and bound states in one-dimensional chains.

title: Dirac Structures and Reduction of Optimal Control Problems with Symmetries
summary: We study the symmetry reduction of optimal control problems using Dirac structures. The first-order conditions of the Pontryagin Maximum Principle are written as an implicit Dirac system on the Pontryagin bundle. For a problem invariant under a Lie group, we reduce both the Lagrange-Pontryagin variational principle and the underlying Dirac structure, and prove that they yield the same reduced equations, which we identify with the Hamiltonian equations on the dual of the Atiyah algebroid. Reconstruction, independence of the principal connection, and the relation between criticality and optimality complete the picture. Dropping regularity, we give the Gotay-Nester-Hinds constraint algorithm a Dirac-geometric form and prove that symmetry reduction commutes with it. For control-linear systems whose admissible directions are horizontal for a principal connection, abnormal extremals lie on the leaf where the base costate vanishes, and the first secondary constraint is the degeneracy of the curvature pairing. We also give a reduced criterion for strict abnormality and a metric-free index form. Examples: a spacecraft with rotors (flat connection), the Heisenberg group (nowhere-zero curvature) and the Martinet problem (curvature vanishing on a hypersurface).

title: Quintaverse-Phantiverse Cosmologies in $f(Q,C)$ Gravity: a Non-coincident Geometrical Origin of Cosmic Acceleration
summary: We investigate the asymptotic dark energy sectors of a quadratic form of $f(Q,C)$ Lagrangian. We reformulate the original equations of motion to obtain the equivalent dynamical system, for two non-trivial classes of affine connections allowed by symmetries of $f(Q,C)$ gravity. In these scenarios, the late-time accelerated expansion emerges as an intrinsic geometrical effect of the $f(Q,C)$ sector, without invoking an independent dark energy component. We find that an effective dark matter solution emerges for one class, whereas for the other class, the positivity of the matter density and the conservation of the momentum tensor cannot be simultaneously satisfied. This leads to the conclusion that there exists an effective dark matter solution for which the matter contribution is a combination of a pressureless matter as well as a stiff fluid. Furthermore, in both cases there always exists a universal stable accelerated expansion solution. Besides, the matter solutions are saddle points for those values of the model parameters that ensure the conservation of the energy momentum. In addition, we introduce a parameterization in which the equation of state parameter at the fixed point corresponding to accelerated expansion is characterized by a free parameter that quantifies its deviation from $-1$. We thereby inspired to invent the terms ``Quintaverse'' and ``Phantiverse'', corresponding to quintessence-like and phantom-like attractor solutions. Also, we numerically illustrate the evolution of different cosmological quantities and the phase-space diagrams. Particularly, the behavior of the Universe using two kinematic toolkits, namely, the cosmographic and statefinder variables, is discussed.

title: Probing Heavy Neutral Leptons through New Gauge Interactions at the Forward Physics Facilities
summary: We investigate the prospects for improving the heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches at the far-forward LHC experiments FASER and FASER$ν$, as well as their proposed HL-LHC successors, FASER2 and FASER$ν$2, using new HNL production mechanisms. We consider scenarios in which HNLs couple directly to a new $U(1)$ gauge boson and decay into visible Standard Model final states through mixing with active neutrinos. Focusing on the $U(1)_{B-L}$, $U(1)_{B-3L_τ}$, and $U(1)_B$ gauge extensions as benchmark models, we study HNL production through proton bremsstrahlung and Drell--Yan processes, which probe complementary mediator-mass regimes. We analyze several visible decay channels, including charged leptons, neutral mesons, and other hadrons, and evaluate the projected sensitivities for different neutrino-flavor mixing patterns. We find that these new production mechanisms that differ qualitatively from the conventional picture in which both production and decay are controlled by active-sterile mixing enable the far-forward LHC program to probe previously unexplored regions of HNL parameter space, with the first-ever demonstration of FASER$ν$ having sensitivity to HNLs and FASER2 and FASER$ν$2 offering substantially enhanced sensitivity during the HL-LHC era, even reaching the canonical seesaw prediction for all three lepton flavors. Our results demonstrate that new gauge interactions can substantially enhance HNL production independently of the active-sterile mixing that governs their visible decays, opening complementary opportunities to explore HNLs at the forward physics facilities.

title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
summary: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

title: Non-Destructive Detection of Early Drought Stress via Spectral Submanifold Analysis
comment: Includes supplementary information and one supplementary video. This manuscript has been submitted
summary: Non-destructive early detection of water stress is critical for precision agriculture, yet current detection methods are often labor-intensive or destructive. We propose a rapid, non-invasive method based on Spectral Submanifold (SSM) reduction to analyze the nonlinear vibration dynamics of soybean plants. Unlike traditional linear modal analysis, our data-driven approach reveals a distinct transition in the dominant dynamics of the plant stem as drought progresses. Specifically, we uncover a sign reversal in the nonlinear damping coefficient within SSM-reduced models of full plants. Our finding reveals a fundamental transition in the plant's dissipative mechanics from a pressurized, fluid-rich vessel exhibiting superlinear (viscoelastic) damping to a dry, cellular solid dominated by sublinear (frictional) damping. This transition is closely correlated with the onset of physiological stress indicated by a significant decrease in the values of mature-leaf soil plant analysis development (SPAD) and colorimetric metrics. In contrast, traditional metrics, such as linear frequency and leaf wilting, do not provide consistent statistical signals of water stress. This study provides the first experimental evidence that SSM-based nonlinear model reduction can detect the changing internal state of a living organism, offering a physics-based metric for high-throughput plant phenotyping.

title: Hadamard states for linearized gravity on asymptotically flat spacetimes
summary: We consider the quantization of linearized Einstein equations on 4-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. We prove the existence of fully gauge invariant Hadamard states in the harmonic gauge for any Einstein metric asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in a conic neighborhood of spatial infinity.

title: Black Hole Shadows and Quasinormal Modes with Dark Matter at the Horizon
summary: In this work, we study the effect of a surrounding dark matter halo on two horizon-scale observables of a black hole: its shadow and quasinormal-mode spectrum. We consider a Schwarzschild black hole embedded in a Hernquist halo and construct a one-parameter family of solutions that preserve the total halo mass while varying how the halo density vanishes at the horizon. By closing the Einstein equations with an Einstein-cluster stress tensor, we show that horizon regularity requires the density to vanish at least linearly. Our results also indicate that the dominant energy condition is violated in a thin layer outside the horizon, highlighting the limitations of the Einstein-cluster description within the photon sphere. We demonstrate that, at fixed black hole mass, the halo always enlarges the shadow, with the effect becoming more pronounced for more massive and compact halos. Comparison with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr\,A$^*$ and M87$^*$ shows that only sufficiently compact halos can be constrained, with the inferred bounds depending sensitively on whether the observed mass is identified with the black hole mass or the total mass of the system. We further show that the halo lowers both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of electromagnetic and axial gravitational quasinormal modes, leading to higher quality factors. These spectral shifts are quantitatively explained by changes in the photon-sphere properties through the eikonal correspondence. Since the effects scale with the ratio of the halo mass to its size, they are observable only for dark matter concentrated within a few tens of gravitational radii of the black hole, which is the regime considered here.

title: Sequential SBI for Resonance Searches at the LHC
summary: Neural simulation-based inference has been shown to extract significantly more information from LHC data than histogram-based analyses. So far, it has mostly been applied to couplings, for which the polynomial structure of the scattering amplitude can be exploited. Masses and widths instead move and deform the signal in phase space, and learning their likelihood requires many event samples covering the continuous theory parameter space. We show how sequential simulation-based inference can address this by iteratively concentrating the simulations where the observed data points. Using a parton-level example with an exact reference likelihood and reconstruction-level analyses of $A\to ZH\to \ell\ell b\bar b$ and $Y\to HH\to (t\bar t)(t\bar t)$, we demonstrate that sequential training produces significantly more accurate and better calibrated likelihoods than single round training with the same amount of training events.

title: Big Crunching Your Big Bang: Doubly Warped Time-Dependent Type II Flux Backgrounds and Scale Separation
summary: We construct three analytic, doubly warped cosmological solutions of massless type IIA supergravity with different choices of fluxes, namely, $H_3$, $\tilde F_2$ and $\tilde F_4$ along internal directions. The $H_3$ solution also belongs to the common NS--NS sector of type IIB. Our solutions show that, without localised sources, nonconstant warping on a smooth compact space is possible. We derive their eleven-dimensional uplifts and four-dimensional Einstein-frame cosmology. Each universe undergoes (decelerating) expansion from a Big Bang, reaches a maximum size, and undergoes contraction towards a Big Crunch. We also analyse the scale separation of these backgrounds and find that they exhibit a small Einstein frame Hubble scale to KK mass ratio $\frac{|H_E|}{m_{\mathrm{KK}}}\ll1,$ although for a brief period of time, around the maxima of the scale factor in the Einstein frame. Finally, we analyse the supersymmetry of these backgrounds, which demonstrates that all three solutions break all forms of type IIA supersymmetry.

title: $π$-Flux Tuning of Quantum Paramagnetism in the Triangular-Lattice Hubbard Model
summary: We compare two time-reversal-symmetric triangular-lattice Hubbard models at half filling: the zero-flux model and a staggered $π$-flux model with zero and $π$ flux through oppositely oriented triangles. Although both reduce to the same Heisenberg model at leading order in the strong-coupling limit, their distinct charge fluctuation profiles yield different quantum paramagnetic regimes. Combining a strong-coupling expansion with infinite density matrix renormalization group (iDMRG) calculations, we find that the positive ring-exchange of the zero-flux model promotes spontaneous chirality, consistent with its notion of a chiral spin liquid at intermediate coupling. In the staggered-$π$-flux model, whose noninteracting limit is a Dirac semimetal, the ring exchange changes sign and disfavors chiral order and we find no resolvable scalar chirality. This renders flux-tuned ring-exchange an efficient discriminator between chiral and non-chiral quantum paramagnets at finite coupling.

title: Symmetric and antisymmetric cumulant hierarchies and Wick polynomials of operators
summary: There has been much progress in understanding mathematical foundations of kinetic theory in recent years, in particular, for the original model of a rarefied gas of classical particles with repulsive interactions, as well as for weakly nonlinear wave evolutions related to wave turbulence. These results are mainly based on refined analysis of evolution hierarchies of moments of the relevant random variables, or of related quantities such as of cumulants or of correlation errors. In this work, we extend two of such basic tools, cumulants and Wick polynomials, to a setting where the random variables no longer need to commute, with the goal of handling expectations of creation and annihilation operators on a Fock space, both in the bosonic and fermionic case. We call these constructions symmetric and antisymmetric cumulants and Wick polynomials, respectively. As an application, we derive a hierarchy of evolution equations satisfied by such cumulants, usually called truncated correlation functions in this context, for a gas of bosons or fermions hopping on a finite lattice and interacting via a two-body potential. With sufficient control over solutions to these hierarchies, one could control the magnitude of the error terms related to an approximation of the state of the quantum system by a finite lattice kinetic equation studied in our earlier work, closely connected to standard bosonic and fermionic Boltzmann--Nordheim equations.

title: Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
summary: A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.

title: Continuous Measurement of Quantum Axion Dark Matter
summary: We provide a fully quantum-mechanical description of the continuous measurement of wavelike dark matter. Our focus is cavity haloscopes, although our results inform a broad range of axion searches. We extend the input-output formalism by treating the axion as a quantum field, finding how its quantum state is imprinted onto higher-order moments of observables of the outgoing transmission-line modes. We further develop a novel measurement-record formalism, which computes the joint probability distribution of all measurement outcomes and is well suited to studying the axion in the time domain. With it, we compute the exact axion-induced number distribution for the first time, demonstrating that it is not Poisson. We argue that virialized axion dark matter is expected to be in a Gaussian quantum state, and show that number or quadrature measurements can distinguish this from the predictions of a coherent state or even a Bose-Einstein condensate. Finally, we show that intrinsically quantum effects, such as those from Fock or squeezed axion states, are far too weak to detect.

title: Pressure in Wilsonian effective field theory
summary: We study the exponential rolling tachyon solution in Wilsonian effective field theory as a model for rolling tachyons in open string field theory. Although this solution exhibits runaway oscillations towards the future similar to its counterparts in string field theory, its pressure is shown to be consistent with the underlying bare theory, but only up to a finite time. The rest of the evolution of the pressure is instead governed by a solution that is oscillatory towards the past and regular at late times. We conjecture that the late time physics of rolling tachyons in open string field theory may be captured by the solutions that are different from the standard rolling tachyon solutions based on this analysis.

title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
summary: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size $N$, which goes from $\mathcal{O}({\rm poly}(N))$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.

title: An elliptic generalization of the $D^{(2)}_{2}$ Spin chain
summary: An integrable elliptic generalization of the closed $D^{(2)}_2$ quantum spin chain is constructed. Taking the trigonometric limit, we have shown that the corresponding R-matrix reduces to that of the $D^{(2)}_2$ one, up to a similarity transformation. Basing on the very fact of the factorization for the R-matrix and the corresponding transfer matrix which indeed ensures the integrability of the model, we give the exact solution of the model which can be expressed in terms of a homogeneous T-Q relation.

title: Perturbations, eikonal limit and Hawking radiation of diverse external fields in a non-minimal charged black hole
summary: We compare the quasinormal modes (QNMs), greybody factors, and Hawking emission of massless scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac test fields propagating on a non-minimal Einstein--Yang--Mills black hole. The QNMs are calculated using WKB and pseudospectral methods, while greybody factors are estimated with sixth-order WKB method. All computed modes are damped within the parameter range considered. Higher overtones generally exhibit stronger dependence on the non-minimal coupling $ξ$ than the fundamental mode, including non-monotonic behavior in the scalar and Dirac sectors. For large multipole numbers, all three fields follow a common leading eikonal description governed by the unstable circular null orbit. Increasing $ξ$ raises the orbital angular velocity and reduces the Lyapunov exponent, leading to higher oscillation frequencies and weaker damping rate. The greybody factors depend strongly on the multipole number, with weaker field dependent corrections from $ξ$. The partial-wave emission powers generally decrease with increasing $ξ$, while the lowest scalar mode shows mild non-monotonic behavior. This comparison reveals enhanced overtone sensitivity alongside comparatively small changes in transmission, whereas the Hawking emission reflects changes in both the greybody factors and the black hole temperature.

title: Neutrino Transition Polarizability
summary: We study Neutrino Transition Polarizability, where a light pseudoscalar $φ$ couples active neutrinos to heavy neutral leptons $N$ and interacts with two photons. We consider an effective description of the active - sterile interaction, and a realization within the inverse seesaw mechanism; the coupling to photons is generated by heavy charged states. For $m_N>m_φ$, the decay $N\toνφ$ can greatly shorten the heavy neutrino lifetime, while $φ\toγγ$ produces a displaced photon pair. This changes the relevant search strategies, favoring production and decay inside detectors. We discuss existing constraints and estimate the sensitivity of displaced photon searches at DUNE, Belle II, LHCb and FCC-ee, highlighting the complementarity of neutrino scattering and meson and electroweak boson decays.

title: Fluids on null hypersurfaces and Carrollian hydrodynamics
summary: We study intrinsic ideal fluids on null hypersurfaces and their realisations by causal fluids living in the ambient spacetime. An embedded null hypersurface is equipped with an induced Carrollian structure with a temporal Weyl symmetry inherited from rescalings of the null generator, and we develop the corresponding null submanifold and variational calculus. The intrinsic fluid phases are classified according to their realisation of Carroll boosts and temporal Weyl symmetry. If we demand that an ambient fluid be confined to a null hypersurface, the ambient fluid velocity must be null, which realises an intrinsic zero-temperature Carrollian phase with unbroken Carroll boosts. In general, timelike or null ambient fluids will cross a null hypersurface and lead to an open Carrollian system. On a null foliation, the sources correspond to transport between null leaves. We then show that there exists a decoupling limit of a timelike ambient fluid which gives rise to an autonomous Carrollian fluid with spontaneously broken Carroll boosts and no source terms. This decoupling limit corresponds to an infinite boost while keeping the enthalpy finite and nonzero, which leads to a divergent ambient energy-momentum tensor. Nevertheless, the induced Carrollian responses do not see the divergent term and remain finite, and an independent Carroll boost Goldstone emerges from a subleading component of the ambient fluid velocity in this limit.

title: Domain walls in $R3c$-structured NaNbO$_3$
summary: In this work, we undertake a systematic first-principles study of structural domain walls in the low-temperature rhombohedral $R3c$ phase of perovskite oxide NaNbO$_3$. Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the $R3c$ structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and charge neutrality, and perform structural relaxations for each representative domain wall class. We find that one class of 109° domain walls has a notably low energy of 9 mJ m$^{-2}$, comparable to the low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO$_3$. Finally, we find that this class of 109° walls is compatible with the crystal twinning observed in experiments on the $R3c$ phase, and propose an atomistic mechanism for the $R3c \leftrightarrow Pbcm$ phase transition.

title: Some minimal characteristics and flat trajectories of a system in the N-body problem
summary: For the classical model of a system of N particles with interaction (the N-body problem) we consider some spatial problems of nonlinear programming for finding conditional minima and local extrema for the main characteristics of the system on its phase space. We prove that these conditional minima and local extrema of the system characteristics can only be achieved on flat, in general, not necessarily finite, trajectories of the system in space, (under the condition that the system angular momentum is non-zero). And then we find the basic conditions limiting the values of the integrals of motion: angular momentum and total energy of the system under which these trajectories are flat finite ("circular" or elliptical) trajectories on which the flat structure of the system is preserved in time under the certain restrictions on the values of the system's integrals of motion. And we determine also the values of the system's key characteristics on these flat trajectories. Next, in the Appendix, we consider some additional related results for a more general model of the system.

title: Multi-orbit S-star probes of Lorentz violation at the Galactic Center
summary: We investigate the potential of Galactic-center S-star observations to probe Lorentz violation in the minimal pure-gravity Standard-Model Extension (SME), focusing on parameter degeneracies associated with anisotropic orbital signatures. We construct simulated astrometric and spectroscopic observations of S2 and S55 using fiducial orbital and Galactic-center parameters based on the multi-star solution from the GRAVITY Collaboration and evolve the stellar trajectories using the leading Lorentz-violating two-body dynamics supplemented by the Schwarzschild first-post-Newtonian (1PN) correction. Separate Fisher-matrix analyses of S2 and S55 each resolve seven of the eight independent SME directions, while their joint analysis resolves all eight directions by combining complementary projections from the differently oriented orbits. A subsequent Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis confirms the Fisher forecasts and reaches characteristic 95% credible-level sensitivities of approximately 10^(-3)-10^(-2) for the time-space components and 10^(-5)-10^(-4) for the spatial components. Our results demonstrate that combining S-stars with different orbital orientations is effective for breaking geometrical degeneracies and probing the tensor structure of Lorentz violation in the Galactic-center gravitational field.

title: Machine Learning Neutrino-Nucleus Cross Sections II: More Leptons
summary: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections are essential inputs for long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, yet remain challenging to model with high precision. Recent work demonstrated that fully black-box data-driven cross-section models cannot accurately generalize between near- and far-detector fluxes, but imposing Standard-Model symmetries via structure-function parameterizations provides a well-posed learning problem in a simplified DUNE-inspired muon-neutrino disappearance analysis. Here, we extend this framework to multiple lepton flavors and both neutrino and antineutrino beam modes, incorporating the electron appearance channel and enabling a simultaneous determination of $\sin^2θ_{23}$, $Δm^2_{31}$, and the CP-violating phase $δ_{\rm CP}$. We find that the learned cross section model recovers the injected oscillation parameters without significant bias, with constraints comparable to those obtained using the exact underlying cross section. Flux uncertainties have more significant effects in the multi-channel case, and incorporating flux nuisance parameters into the learning problem is required for accurate results. Our results demonstrate that this data-driven approach can be extended to the multi-channel measurements needed for long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses.

title: Maxwell-Chern-Simons-Matter in AdS$_3$
summary: We study Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory on AdS$_3$ coupled to $N$ complex scalars or Dirac fermions, including sextic and Gross-Neveu interactions, respectively. First, we derive the bulk Maxwell-Chern-Simons propagator, clarifying how Dirichlet boundary conditions fix the contributions of the massive and flat sectors. Upon coupling to the matter sector, we work at large $N$ with $κ=k/N$ and $α=Ne^2$ fixed, where $k$ is the Chern-Simons level. We determine the corresponding phase diagrams, and we resum matter insertions to obtain the photon propagator at leading order in large $N$, exactly in $α$ and $κ$. Its poles determine the spin-one boundary spectrum, split into two helicity sectors by the Chern-Simons interaction. With Dirichlet boundary conditions, the unHiggsed scalar phase contains a protected chiral current, which is lifted by Higgsing. In the fermionic phases, the current persists for nonzero effective Chern-Simons level, with helicity determined by the induced level shift. At bulk conformal points, we extract large-$N$ BCFT data for the critical and tricritical scalar theories, as well as for the regular fermion and Gross-Neveu theories.

title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
summary: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

title: Mutual transformations of arbitrary ternary qubit trees by Clifford gates
summary: It is shown that ternary qubit trees with the same number of nodes can be transformed by the naturally defined sequence of Clifford gates into each other or into standard representation as one-dimensional chain corresponding to Jordan-Wigner transform.

title: Decoherence of the quantum superradiant cloud from graviton emission
summary: Black hole superradiance amplifies vacuum fluctuations into a macroscopic cloud of a massive bosonic field around a rotating black hole. Under free evolution, the quantum cloud is a two-mode squeezed state that remains entangled even at large occupation numbers, while its growing component admits a classical statistical description. In this work, we study how graviton emission changes the quantum state of the cloud. We find that graviton emission suppresses interference between cloud configurations with different amplitudes, but leaves interference between configurations that differ only by an overall sign unchanged. For typical configurations realized under vacuum fluctuations, the suppression becomes significant when the expected number of emitted gravitons is of order unity.We also show that, at larger occupation numbers, all first and second moments can be reproduced by a statistical mixture of coherent states. For the astrophysical black holes, both changes occur much before the spin-down of the black hole becomes significant.

title: What if dark matter is composite of least interacting particles?
summary: In this work, we investigate the possibility that Dark Matter contains particles that interact with known matter only through gravity, the least interacting particles (LIPs). Specifically, we consider the case of a dark Proca vector field, which does not mix in the kinetic term with any of the vector bosons of the Standard Model if a discrete symmetry (Z2 ) is imposed. Breaking this symmetry introduces kinetic mixing. Here, we study two realization mechanisms, namely kinetic mixing with the electromagnetic field after electroweak symmetry breaking (Scenario A) and kinetic mixing with the weak hypercharge gauge field (Scenario B). We also consider generalized kinetic terms that violate parity and time-reversal symmetries.

title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
summary: We derive the primordial $\langleζζh\rangle$, $\langleζhh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.

title: Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
summary: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.

title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
comment: 81 pages, 34 figures, 1 Mathematica notebook in the ancillary files
summary: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints.
